claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 15 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great. A few more questions:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you or your partner (if you have one) a Crown servant, or do you have any special immigration status such as pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually I have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, I need to ask a few additional questions to determine your eligibility.

Which of the following applies to your current situation?

1. You're working (earning or expecting to earn above the National Insurance primary threshold for 3 continuous months)
2. You're looking for work
3. You have sufficient resources to support yourself financially (without claiming Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit or Universal Credit)
4. You're studying with sufficient resources to support yourself
5. You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national who has a right to reside

Which category best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about all those specific categories. I work, if that helps - I have a regular job.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Just to confirm for the pre-settled status requirements:

Are you earning (or do you expect to earn) above the National Insurance primary threshold? This is currently around £242 per week or about £1,048 per month. Have you been working at this level for at least 3 continuous months, or do you expect to?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about the exact threshold amount or whether I've been earning above it for three months. I just know I have a regular job, but I don't have all those specific details about my earnings and National Insurance thresholds to hand.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's completely understandable. Let me ask you this in a simpler way:

Do you have a regular, ongoing job where you work enough hours that you pay National Insurance contributions? This would typically be if you're earning more than around £240-250 per week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know the specifics of my National Insurance contributions or exactly how much I earn per week. I just have a job, but I don't have those financial details with me right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - those details can be hard to recall off the top of your head. Let me ask this differently:

Approximately how many hours per week do you work, and roughly what is your salary or hourly wage? This will help me determine if you likely meet the earnings threshold.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm sorry, I really don't have those details available right now. I know I work, but I can't give you specific hours or wages off the top of my head.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine. Let me work with what we know so far.

Based on the information you've provided:
- You have a 15-year-old child (Alex) who lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex and no one else is claiming Child Benefit
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have a regular job

The main uncertainty is whether your employment meets the specific earnings threshold required for pre-settled status holders (earning above the National Insurance primary threshold for 3 continuous months).

Without being able to confirm your specific earnings details, I cannot make a definitive determination on your eligibility. However, I can tell you:

**If** you are earning above approximately £242 per week (the National Insurance primary threshold) and have been doing so for at least 3 continuous months, then you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

I'd recommend:
1. Checking your payslips to confirm your earnings, or
2. Proceeding with a Child Benefit application - HMRC will assess whether you meet the earnings requirement as part of processing your claim

Is there anything else about your situation that might be relevant, or would you like me to make an assessment based on what we've discussed?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. So just to be clear - if my earnings are above that threshold and I've been working for three months, then I would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, right? Since he's 15, lives with me, and nobody else is claiming for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct! Let me confirm the key points:

**If your earnings meet the threshold** (above approximately £242 per week for 3 continuous months), then you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because:

- Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- You live in the UK

The only condition specific to your situation is the earnings requirement due to your pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

Since you've confirmed you have a regular job but can't verify the specific earnings details right now, I cannot make a completely definitive eligibility determination. However, **if** your earnings are above that threshold, you would meet all the requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

Would you like me to provide a formal assessment based on what we've discussed, noting that eligibility depends on confirming your earnings meet the threshold?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that would be helpful. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

## Summary of Eligibility Assessment for Alex

**Eligibility Status: INDETERMINATE**

You meet all the basic requirements for Child Benefit:
- Alex is 15 years old (under 16) ✓
- Alex lives with you in the UK ✓
- You're responsible for Alex ✓
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex ✓

**However**, because you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, there's an additional requirement: you must be earning above the National Insurance primary threshold (approximately **£242 per week** or about **£1,048 per month**) for 3 continuous months.

Since you couldn't confirm your specific earnings details today, I cannot make a definitive determination.

### Next Steps:
1. **Check your payslips** to see if you're earning above £242 per week
2. **If you are**, you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex
3. You can proceed with your application, and HMRC will verify your earnings as part of the process

You're welcome! If you have any other questions or can provide those earnings details later, please feel free to reach out.
